title: Machine Learning Model with Fourier-Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) as a Proof-of-Concept Tool for Predicting Group A Streptococcus (GAS) emm-Type in the Pediatric Population.
summary: Fourier-transform infrared spectra from 24 pediatric group A Streptococcus isolates were classified by machine learning. In the 21-strain, four-emm-type evaluation, the artificial neural network reached 90.7% accuracy; three isolates from unseen emm types received low-confidence assignments. This is a small proof of concept, not a validated unknown-class rejection system. The bibliographic records retrieved do not state an author affiliation.
ai_technology: IR Biotyper machine-learning classifiers applied to FTIR spectra; the artificial neural network had the strongest reported accuracy.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: The ANN achieved 90.7% accuracy (89.9% sensitivity, 98.2% specificity, F1 0.92) in leave-one-out cross-validation over 21 strains and four emm types; three out-of-type strains were separately assessed.
evidence.unknown: The sample was small; low confidence on three unseen emm types does not establish reliable rejection of unknown classes. Multicenter validation was not reported.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning classifiers analyzed FTIR spectra to predict the emm type of pediatric group A Streptococcus isolates.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
